newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Trade volumes boost Australia GDP -analysis.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Trade volumes boost Australia GDP -analysis.

text.p: September quarter trade and price data suggest that net exports will contribute 0.4 percentage points to quarterly growth in Australian GDP.
The contribution stems from stronger nominal exports and slightly weaker nominal imports.
Adjusted for price changes, a picture emerges of rising export volumes working in unison with substantially lower import volumes.
Quarterly balance of payments data is not yet available. Monthly data can be used, but the figures have to be adjusted for seasonality and price changes.
For seasonality, some economists apply the seasonal adjustment used in the same quarter last year to the original data shown in the monthly releases.
The method assumes no significant compositional changes but is usually accurate to within 0.1 percent of GDP. It was, however, quite inaccurate in the June quarter.
Price movements are indicated by the export and import price indexes, September values for which were published on Friday to imply a price deflator.

After adjusting the original trade data for both effects, September quarter exports of goods and services appear to be A$25.31 billion in 1989/90 currency used in GDP figures, up A$138 million from from A$25.18 billion in the June quarter.
Since A$138 million is about 0.1 percent of quarterly GDP, the implied contribution to quarterly GDP growth is 0.1 percent.
Constant price imports appear to be A$24.81 billion, A$304 million higher than the June data and implying a contribution of 0.3 percent.
The net effect of exports and imports together is an estimated A$442 million or 0.4-percentage-point contribution to quarterly GDP growth.
